findings.title: No backend / serverless function — blocks any keyed AI or 3rd-party API call
evidence: server/briefing-worker.js — Cloudflare Worker proxy (Anthropic Claude), default-off
briefing-llm.js — client enhancer with deterministic fallback
server/README.md deploy runbook; docs/intelligence/AI_STACK.md architecture+cost
key held as a Wrangler secret, never in the repo or browser

history.note: Baseline. Hard prerequisite for the LLM path of OPP-002 and for OPP-004. A static site cannot safely hold a model key. Not a bug — a boundary condition.

Phase 4 (v1.5.0): a deployable serverless backend path now EXISTS in the repo (Cloudflare Worker + client integration + runbook + cost model), unblocking keyed AI. Marked in-progress not resolved because it is default-off and not deployed — activation needs the owner's Cloudflare account + ANTHROPIC_API_KEY. Resolves once deployed.

Added one-command deploy automation (npm run deploy:briefing -> server/deploy.mjs) + optional CI workflow. Reduces activation to a Cloudflare browser-auth + pasting the API key; the script auto-wires the worker URL into index.html. Still in-progress until the owner actually runs it (their account/key/cost).

Decided against by the owner: the product is intentionally PURELY STATIC. The only thing that ever needed a backend was optional LLM rephrasing of the briefing, which was over-engineered for a read-only dashboard that already refreshes itself live from the MLB API on every load. All Cloudflare/worker/deploy scaffolding + the client LLM enhancer were removed (v1.15.0). Revisitable later via a build-time JSON-precompute pattern (scheduled CI -> committed briefing.json) with no runtime server, if richer phrasing is ever wanted.

findings.title: No data persistence / historical accumulation — no day-over-day memory
evidence: history-engine.js — daily standings snapshots in localStorage (rolling ~30d)
diffRanks shows rank movement (up/down) vs the most recent prior day in the Daily standings
per-browser, client-side; no durable/server-side accumulation for ML

history.note: Baseline. Removes the basis for predictive AI (no owned training data) and multi-season browsing.

v1.14.0: day-over-day MEMORY shipped (history-engine.js, 7 tests). Standings are snapshotted daily to localStorage and diffed against the prior day to show rank movement (▲/▼) in the Daily standings; browser-verified (NYY ▲1 / BOS ▼1 from a seeded yesterday). In-progress not resolved: the *day-over-day* need is met, but durable/multi-season historical accumulation for predictive AI (per RISK-002) is still absent — that needs the GAP-001 backend / a real datastore.

findings.title: No telemetry / analytics — zero signal on what users view
evidence: telemetry.js — local per-feature counts (localStorage) + optional default-off beacon
wired to load/tab/theme/scoreboard events; window.__telemetry() inspector
no aggregate collector deployed (static site has no default backend)

history.note: Baseline. Prerequisite for personalization/recommendations and for evidence-based prioritization of OPP-004 (Q&A).

v1.13.0: privacy-light instrumentation layer added (telemetry.js, 8 tests). Always-on LOCAL counts via window.__telemetry() give immediate per-feature signal; network beaconing is default-OFF (no PII/cookies) and lights up only when a telemetry-endpoint meta tag points at a collector. In-progress not resolved: aggregate analytics still needs a deployed collector (same backend gap as GAP-001).

findings.title: Hard dependency on unauthenticated public MLB Stats API (single point of failure)
evidence: data-client.js:17 API_BASE statsapi.mlb.com
api-cache.js — network-first sessionStorage cache with stale fallback (≤6h)
degraded 'showing cached data' notice; still no secondary data source

history.note: Baseline. If MLB changes/rate-limits/retires the undocumented public endpoints, the whole app goes dark. Mitigated only by a graceful error banner (app.js:429), not by resilience. Off-season also yields sparse/empty data.

v1.12.0: materially MITIGATED — network-first cache with stale fallback (api-cache.js) means a transient failure serves the last good data instead of blanking the page (covers the new live-polling path too), with an auto-clearing degraded notice. 7 tests + browser-verified. Residual risk remains: a permanent/long (>6h) outage or a breaking API change still has no second source. Kept in-progress (mitigated, not eliminated).

findings.title: Trends chart canvas grew/collapsed unbounded (Chart.js responsive feedback loop)
evidence: Chart.js responsive:true + maintainAspectRatio:false in a flex .trends-body with indeterminate height
canvas height fed back into layout -> collapse (58px) or unbounded growth
home-road logo strip lived inside the canvas container, compounding the issue

history.note: Reported by user: Trends UI bug causing an infinitely growing chart.

v1.5.2: gave chart bodies a definite 280px height with the canvas absolutely filling it (Chart.js's documented container requirement); moved the home/road strip to a sibling below the body. Verified in-browser: canvas stable at 280px across 0-4.7s samples, no growth/collapse. Scoped via :has(> canvas) so table/heatmap bodies are untouched.

User still saw growth after 1.5.2: the fix was masked by (a) stale CSS cache — styles.css had no cache-busting, so the old stylesheet kept loading while the HTML version marker updated; and (b) reliance on the :has() selector. The code fix was correct but didn't reach the browser.

v1.5.3: hardened — chart containers carry an explicit .trends-body--chart class (no :has() dependency), asset URLs are version-cache-busted (styles.css?v=, app.js?v=), and a hard max-height:280px backstop added. Verified in-browser: class rule applies, CSS loads fresh, canvases stable at 280px.

findings.title: 'Network hiccup' degraded banner showing almost constantly
evidence: User report: banner shows all the time regardless of console output
api-cache emits 'degraded' on every cache fallback, even a fresh-cache blip on the 30-120s scoreboard poll; error caught silently so no console trace

history.note: The resilience cache serves a fallback (and emits 'degraded') on ANY failed fetch, including a momentary blip on the recurring live-scoreboard poll that returns a cache only seconds old. The fetch error is swallowed inside the cache layer, so nothing logs, yet the banner fires — and with the poll looping it never clears.

v1.20.0: 'degraded' now carries the served cache age + url. The banner shows only when data is meaningfully stale (>5 min) and clears the instant any fetch succeeds; sub-minute fallbacks are silent. A console.debug names the stale url/age when it does appear. New unit test pins the degraded(age,url) contract; suite 93. Browser-verified: fresh-blip stays hidden, 10-min-stale shows, recovery clears.
